subject: Initial response lag & streaming specs — FinOS pilot
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finos.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 22:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial response lag & streaming specs — FinOS pilot

Hi Elena,

Great to be on the call earlier — thanks for walking through the FinOS ingestion use cases. Quick written recap and a set of concrete asks so we can scope a short pilot: 

1) TL;DR SLO targets you gave:
   - Time-to-first-token (TTFT) objective: p95 <= 300ms for streaming responses (user-facing dashboards).
   - End-to-end tail target: p99 <= 700ms for single-turn queries (no heavy external lookups).
   - Concurrency & throughput: baseline 150 concurrent active streams, with planned bursts to ~350 during batch-report windows.

2) Streaming characteristics you described:
   - SSE preferred for browser dashboards; WebSocket is acceptable for internal infra.
   - Expected chunk cadence: small chunks (40–80 tokens) emitted frequently — roughly every 80–140ms for live progress; occasionally larger summary chunks.

3) Constraints & risk flags from our side to confirm:
   - Payload size: many queries include 6–12k of context (user history + report snippet) — we’ll need to discuss KV cache behavior.
   - Quality vs latency tradeoffs: you mentioned willingness to try 8-bit quantized variants if p95 TTFT improves.

Next steps I propose:
- You share a representative set of 50 sample requests and a few synthetic burst patterns (we can accept the finos_latency_samples.jsonl attachment).
- FinOS sign-off on a pilot window: 2 weeks, with a canary 24–48h headstart (we'll instrument metrics).
- Redwood to produce a short runbook with suggested chunk size / pacing and a failover policy (SSE -> non-streaming fallback).

I attached an initial checklist (FinOS_Tech_Reqs.xlsx) that I’ll update as we lock details.

If this matches your memory, can you confirm the SLO targets and drop the sample file? Once we receive samples we’ll run a small lab pass to validate TTFT at our end and return a recommended config.

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@finos.io>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:15:34 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial response lag & streaming specs — FinOS pilot

Thanks Tessa — that recap is spot on. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT target: we said p95 <= 300ms for the dashboard main card; for background batch generation the p95 requirement is looser (<= 600ms). Can you split these two in the pilot report?
- Concurrency: the 150 concurrent streams is conservative — we typically see that during peak dashboards, but during month-end it's closer to 320 sustained for 2–3 hours. We can provide a weekend burst trace.
- Chunk cadence: the product team prefers more frequent micro-chunks for smoother UX (ideally ~60–100ms cadence). We're flexible on tokens-per-chunk; UX cares more about visual progress.

I attached the latency samples (finos_latency_samples.jsonl) and the tech reqs spreadsheet. For legal/procurement: we might need a short statement of data handling (SLA/retention) before procurement kicks off — I CC'd procurement in case they want to weigh in.

Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Product Engineering, FinOS Labs
elena@finos.io
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finos.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:45:20 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial response lag & streaming specs — FinOS pilot

Elena — great, thanks for the samples and the extra context. Confirming our plan:

Pilot scope (2 weeks):
- Canary (24–48h): run 10% of traffic from FinOS staging through Redwood-hosted config to validate TTFT and chunk cadence.
- Lab pass: Redwood will replay the 50 sample traces and the burst trace you offered; we'll produce a per-path report that splits: dashboard-main-card vs background jobs.
- Metrics we'll report:
   * TTFT p50/p95/p99 (ms)
   * chunk cadence distribution (ms) and average tokens/chunk
   * sustained concurrent streams and peak QPS during replay
   * error rate and fallback occurrences (SSE -> non-stream fallback)

Configuration suggestions we'll test:
- Chunk size/pacing: start with 40 tokens / 80ms cadence, then 60 tokens / 100ms run to compare perceived latency.
- KV caching TTL: 30m for active user sessions, with hot-key pinning for heavy reports.
- Quantization variants: test fp16 and 8-bit quantized model to measure TTFT impact.

Procurement note: we can provide a short data handling note and a pilot statement of work. Laura — can you draft the pilot SOW and a 1-paragraph data handling note (retention, logs, encryption at rest) we can share with procurement?

Elena — once Laura drops the short docs, we can schedule the canary and agree on an exact start date (we're good to start as early as next Tuesday).

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: [Internal] FinOS pilot — SLO focus & ops checklist

Folks — looping you in to operationalize the FinOS pilot. Key asks from the thread above: 

- Primary SLOs: TTFT p95 <= 300ms (dashboard-main-card) and p95 <= 600ms (background jobs).
- Expected concurrency: baseline 150, burst to 320 sustained for short windows.
- Streaming: SSE preferred; we should support WebSocket fallback. Aim to test 40/60 token chunk configurations and report chunk cadence (ms).

Action items: 
- Marcus: build a lightweight replay harness for the finos_latency_samples.jsonl file and generate baseline TTFT numbers for fp16 vs quantized 8-bit. Deliverable: CSV with p50/p95/p99 by model variant, plus chunk cadence histogram. Deadline: 2026-02-16 EOD.
- Rishi: draft a failover policy (SSE -> non-streaming) and the instrumentation hooks to capture fallback reasons. Include a plan to expose these metrics to FinOS console. Deadline: 2026-02-15.
- Laura: draft the 1-page SOW and the short data handling note for procurement and attach to HubSpot deal RDW-DEAL-2026-019. Deadline: 2026-02-13.

I'll coordinate canary windows with Elena once we have the lab pass results. CC'd Elena to keep transparency.

Thanks — Tessa
